| [THEORY-079](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-079.md) v3 | Laplace BMR misprices singular reductions | The filer's synthesis, stated by no source. BMR's closed form (Friston & Penny, [LIT-620](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-620.md), Eq. 9; Friston, Parr & Zeidman, [LIT-614](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-614.md), Eq. 11) charges a reduction through log-determinants of Gaussian precisions, which is MacKay's regular Occam factor. Watanabe, [LIT-616](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-616.md), says that models with hierarchical layers or hidden variables are singular, that no normal distribution approximates their posterior, and that their free energy grows as λ log n. BMR is applied to exactly such models: mixtures, hierarchical empirical Bayes and latent states. Neither literature cites the other. The exact identity is untouched ([THEORY-081](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-081.md)). The claim is about its Laplace form, and a test on reduced-rank regression would settle it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-080](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-080.md) v4 | NTK eigenvalues schedule the Occam penalty | The filer's synthesis, stated by no source. Its exact half is filed as the record's own claim, CLAIM-384; what stays here is the spherical account. A network linearised at initialisation, with an isotropic Gaussian prior on its parameters and Gaussian noise, is MacKay's linear-in-parameters model ([LIT-623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-623.md)). Its Occam factor is −½ Σ log(1 + βλ_a/α) over the eigenvalues of JᵀJ. These are the empirical NTK's, which on uniform spherical data form Bietti & Bach's degree blocks, nµ_k with multiplicity N(d, k) ([LIT-608](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-608.md)). Degrees whose βnµ_k exceeds α pay about ½ log n per harmonic, and degrees below pay almost nothing. With µ_k ~ k^(−d), the number of paid directions γ grows as n^((d−1)/d), not as the parameter count. Basri et al.'s bound ([LIT-612](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-612.md), Eq. 14) is the matching data-fit term. The kernel's decay exponent is the schedule of the penalty. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-081](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-081.md) v2 | Reduced-model evidence is a prior-ratio average | Friston & Penny (2011), [LIT-620](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-620.md), Eq. 3: if models share a likelihood and differ only in priors nested inside a full prior, then p(y\|m_i) = p(y\|m_F)·E_{p(θ\|y,m_F)}[p_i(θ)/p_F(θ)]. Their Eq. 6 is the point-mass case, the Savage–Dickey ratio that Wagenmakers et al. (2010), [LIT-609](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-609.md), derive from the other end, and that Dickey (1971), LIT-610, stated in this form for any continuous likelihood. Friston, Parr & Zeidman, [LIT-614](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-614.md), restate it for any new prior and give conjugate closed forms. Active because the identity is three lines of Bayes' rule that anyone can check. The two Savage–Dickey conditions turn out to be the same condition. The identity is exact. Its Laplace and variational forms are only as good as the full posterior, and with no constraint on the prior family the optimum is maximum likelihood. | Active |
| [THEORY-087](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md) v4 | Singular models pay λ log n, below d/2 | MacKay (1992), [LIT-623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-623.md), writes the evidence as best-fit likelihood times an Occam factor, the ratio of posterior to prior accessible volume, which under a Gaussian approximation is P(w_MP)(2π)^{k/2} det^{-1/2}A. When the likelihood dominates, det A grows as n^d, so the penalty is (d/2) log n. Watanabe's WBIC paper, [LIT-616](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-616.md), recovers that case (Lemma 3, Theorem 5) and states what replaces it when the Fisher information is degenerate at the optimum: λ log n − (m − 1) log log n, with λ the RLCT (Theorem 2). The regular half is re-derived by Laplace's method with its conditions. The singular half is Watanabe's cited theorem, checked by exact free energies in two singular models of known λ. The volume reading of λ is in Watanabe's book, which is unread. | Active |
| [THEORY-259](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-259.md) v3 | Ideal MDL and MAP agree when data are random | Vitányi & Li (1999/2000), [LIT-225](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-225.md), read in [NOTE-801](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-801.md). With the universal prior m and a recursive family Pr(·\|·), −log Pr(D\|H) − log m(H) = K(D\|H) + K(H) + d(D\|H) + O(1), where d(D\|H) = log(m(D\|H)/Pr(D\|H)) is the universal randomness deficiency of D for H; d ≥ −K(Pr(·\|·)) − O(1), and d is bounded exactly when D is Martin-Löf random for H. So ideal MDL and MAP agree to within a constant on admissible hypotheses (Theorems 3–5, re-derived by the record) and part where the data are not random for the hypothesis (0ⁿ against the fair coin). The paper's slack α = K(Pr(·\|H)) + K(P) is an upper bound, not the gap. | Active |
| [THEORY-564](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-564.md) v2 | Model can grow its own structure, unreliably | Smith, Schwartenbeck, Parr and Friston (2020), [LIT-615](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-615.md), read in [NOTE-485](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-485.md). Expansion works in the toy domain over eight runs per condition, and only for novel stimuli. Reduction is the weak half: over 100 runs, the true number of concepts won in 45–80% of runs for four to seven, never for two or three, and in every run when the likelihood was given. Table 1 is the record's only measurement of how often reduction picks the generating structure when the parent model was itself learned. One initialisation; eight concepts, six binary features. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-624](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-624.md) v3 | Agent-or-device is observer-relative | Orseau, McGill & Legg (2018), [LIT-911](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-911.md), read in [NOTE-705](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-705.md). A formal version of Dennett's choice of stance: the posterior probability that a system is an agent, from mixtures of goal-optimizing (inverse RL) and input-output descriptions. Illustrated on seven gridworld trajectories, with no human study. | [THEORY-718](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-718.md) | Evidence is likelihood times an Occam factor | MacKay (1992), [LIT-623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-623.md), Eqs. 5–6 with Eqs. 16 and 19–20, read in [NOTE-471](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-471.md): for y = Φw + noise with Gaussian noise of precision β and the prior w ~ N(0, α⁻¹I) on k weights, the posterior is exactly Gaussian, so the evidence is exactly P(D\|w_MP) times the Occam factor P(w_MP)(2π)^{k/2} det^{-1/2}A, with A = αI + βΦᵀΦ. If ΦᵀΦ/n converges to a positive-definite matrix and w_MP stays bounded, the log Occam factor is −(k/2) log n + O(1). Exact for this model class only. The general regular case and the singular case are [THEORY-087](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md), which is Proposed. | Active |

| [THEORY-1275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1275.md) v2 | SGD transitions only partly match the posterior | Chen, Lau, Mendel, Wei and Murfet (2023), [LIT-1894](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1894.md), read in [NOTE-1462](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1462.md). Their Bayesian antecedent hypothesis is one-way: training's transitions have Bayesian counterparts. From their numbers the antecedents of the chain 4⁺⁺⁻ → 4⁺ → 5 → 5⁺ fall at n ≈ 190, 370 and 1,600–2,500, rising with training. But the posterior's transition 5 → 6 at n ≈ 600 was not seen in training, and SGD on 1000 samples ends at the 5-gon, a 4-gon variant or the 5⁺-gon, none of which the posterior at n = 1000 favours; it favours the 6-gon. The rising order holds at the point estimates, not across the estimates' spread. One model, one SGD setting, estimated learning coefficients; the computation was re-run by a second checker on 2026-11-06 (scratch/formal/tms_critical_sizes_check.py). | Active |

| [THEORY-2155](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2155.md) | Hyperribbon widths track Jacobian singular values | Transtrum, Machta and Sethna (2011), [LIT-3009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3009.md), read in [NOTE-2247](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2247.md). | [THEORY-2166](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2166.md) | Geodesics to manifold edges reduce sloppy models | Transtrum and Qiu (2014), [LIT-2979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2979.md), read in [NOTE-2253](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2253.md). | [THEORY-2237](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2237.md) | Choosing in a series raises patience | Schuhr (2015), [LIT-3114](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3114.md), read in part in [NOTE-2327](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2327.md) for [LEAD-078](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-078.md). In eight one-session treatments of about thirty students each, a free series of decisions raised the mixture probability of exponential discounting by 0.307 (p = 0.019), forcing the decisions together lowered it by 0.330, and stake size did not explain it. Evidence for bundling in humans without an imposed bundle; not for bundling by self-prediction, since every decision in the series is made at once. | Proposed |
